Ava (docs): heads up — I'm about to land a small docs PR that adds an SDK variant and local repro for 429 testing. Need clarity on which snippet permutations we want and the canonical runbook link.
Sam (sdk): thanks, can you paste the minimal repro you used locally? I'll mirror that in sdk-snippets tests.
Ava (docs): here's what triggered the soft 429 on my replay rig: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV' \\
  -H 'X-RateLimit-Test: true' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  --data-raw '{"model":"rwd-1-small","prompt":"repeat x100","max_tokens":1024}'
```
Sam (sdk): nice. for CI we should prefer the throttle helper so tests don't rely on special headers. runtime exposes /test/throttle?rate=5pps for synthetic 429s.
Jordan (runtime): correct — header is convenient locally but the helper is the canonical e2e approach. we should include both examples in docs so contributors can reproduce either way.
Ava (docs): agreed. also want a short example for context-limit fallback (how we trim and show the user that context_truncated happened).
Taylor (qa): i'll run the QA harness against both snippets. one note: the current runbook link in the draft points to /docs/errors/too-many-requests — that's an old alias. we should redirect to /docs/troubleshooting/429 and add the backoff examples there.
Sam (sdk): i'll add an exponential-backoff-with-jitter snippet to the SDK docs. proposed JS snippet: 
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
async function generateWithRetry(req){
  for(let i=0;i<4;i++){
    try{
      return await client.generate(req);
    }catch(e){
      if(e.code !== 'TOO_MANY_REQUESTS') throw e;
      const delay = Math.pow(2,i) * 100 + Math.floor(Math.random()*100);
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries exceeded');
}
```
Ava (docs): perfect. also please add e.context_truncated handling to that sample so folks can detect and trim.
Jordan (runtime): runtime will set context_truncated boolean on responses when we drop earliest tokens to fit model window. i'll add a short note in the runtime section and link to the prompt-trim helper. Sam — can you confirm SDK surfaces e.context_truncated?
Sam (sdk): confirmed, SDK surfaces e.context_truncated on response metadata. i'll add a tiny helper that drops oldest messages until under token threshold and include it inline.
Taylor (qa): QA found a nit: the curl example uses single quotes around JSON which breaks on Windows CMD. suggest adding a PowerShell-friendly example as well.
Ava (docs): good catch. i'll include both curl and PowerShell examples. also can someone run a link-check before merge? last time internal anchors broke a few links.
ci-bot: link-checker job queued for branch refs/heads/docs/429-snippet-variants
Sam (sdk): once CI passes, please route the PR to product-docs for a quick readthrough — small wording tweaks might be needed around "graceful degradation" behavior. @Jordan @Taylor
Jordan (runtime): fine by me. i'll skim the runtime bits.
Taylor (qa): i'll approve after CI and a quick run of the QA harness.

- add header + throttle-helper variants
- add SDK backoff+jitter snippet
- include context_truncated mention + prompt-trim helper
- add PowerShell curl example
- update runbook links and run link-checker
Sam (sdk): thanks all.
Taylor (qa): closing on my side.
Ava (docs): thanks team — closing thread :tada:
